{{Short description|Conjecture in ergodic theory}}
{{distinguish|Aldous' spectral gap conjecture}}

In [[ergodic theory]], a branch of mathematics, the '''spectral gap conjecture''' of [[Alexander Lubotzky]], [[Ralph S. Phillips]], and [[Peter Sarnak]] is a statement on the spectral gaps of certain actions of a [[free group]] on the sphere <math>S^{2}</math>.<ref name="w241">{{cite journal | last1=Lubotzky | first1=A. | last2=Phillips | first2=R. | last3=Sarnak | first3=P. | title=Hecke operators and distributing points on S 2 . II | journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics | volume=40 | issue=4 | date=1987 | issn=0010-3640 | doi=10.1002/cpa.3160400402 | pages=401–420 | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpa.3160400402 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Statement ==
Any matrix <math>U \in SU(2)</math> defines an isometry of the sphere <math>S^{2}</math>, which in turn defines an operator <math>\phi_{U}</math> on the [[Hilbert space]] <math>L^{2}(SU(2))</math>. The spectral gap conjecture states that for any integer <math>n > 2</math>, if <math>n</math> isometries <math>U_{1}, \dots, U_{n}</math> are chosen uniformly at random, then the operator <math>\phi_{U_{1}} + \phi_{U_{1}}^{-1} + \cdots + \phi_{U_{n}} + \phi_{U_{n}}^{-1}</math> has a nontrivial [[spectral gap]] with probability 1.<ref name="w241">{{cite journal | last1=Lubotzky | first1=A. | last2=Phillips | first2=R. | last3=Sarnak | first3=P. | title=Hecke operators and distributing points on S 2 . II | journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics | volume=40 | issue=4 | date=1987 | issn=0010-3640 | doi=10.1002/cpa.3160400402 | pages=401–420 | url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cpa.3160400402 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Progress ==
In 2007, [[Jean Bourgain]] and Alex Gamburd proved that when the matrices <math>U_{i}</math> have entries which are all [[algebraic number]]s up to simultaneous conjugation, the resulting operator has a spectral gap.<ref name="k697">{{cite journal | last1=Bourgain | first1=Jean | last2=Gamburd | first2=Alex | title=On the spectral gap for finitely-generated subgroups of SU(2) | journal=Inventiones mathematicae | volume=171 | issue=1 | date=2007-11-29 | issn=0020-9910 | doi=10.1007/s00222-007-0072-z | pages=83–121 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00222-007-0072-z | url-access=subscription }}</ref> This result was later generalized to the case of <math>SU(d)</math>.<ref name="y478">{{cite journal | last1=Bourgain | first1=Jean | last2=Gamburd | first2=Alex | title=A spectral gap theorem in SU$(d)$ | journal=Journal of the European Mathematical Society | volume=14 | issue=5 | date=2012-08-29 | issn=1435-9855 | doi=10.4171/jems/337 | pages=1455–1511 | url=https://ems.press/doi/10.4171/jems/337 | arxiv=1108.6264 }}</ref> It is known that either there is a nontrivial spectral gap with probability 1 or that the spectral gap is trivial with probability 1.<ref name="h454">{{cite journal | last=Fisher | first=D. | title=Out(Fn) and the spectral gap conjecture | journal=International Mathematics Research Notices | date=2006-01-01 | issn=1073-7928 | doi=10.1155/IMRN/2006/26028 | doi-access=free | page=}}</ref> If true, the statement would have applications to [[quantum computing]] and the design of universal quantum gate sets.<ref name="o408">{{cite journal | last1=Sawicki | first1=Adam | last2=Karnas | first2=Katarzyna | title=Criteria for universality of quantum gates | journal=Physical Review A | volume=95 | issue=6 | date=2017-06-05 | issn=2469-9926 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.95.062303 | url=http://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.95.062303 | arxiv=1610.00547 }}</ref><ref name="p514">{{cite journal | last1=Dulian | first1=Piotr | last2=Sawicki | first2=Adam | title=A Random Matrix Model for Random Approximate t -Designs | journal=IEEE Transactions on Information Theory | volume=70 | issue=4 | date=2024 | issn=0018-9448 | doi=10.1109/TIT.2024.3367787 | pages=2637–2654 | url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10440373/ | arxiv=2210.07872}}</ref>
